# I'd Rather Be Writing

> A technical writing blog and course site by Tom Johnson, a technical writer in the Seattle area (currently at Google, previously Amazon). Running since 2006, the site covers technical communication, API documentation, AI-assisted documentation workflows, and the practice and profession of tech comm. It combines a long-running blog ({{ site.posts | size }} posts) with several free, book-length courses.

The site has two kinds of content:

- **Courses** — structured, sequential, book-length material that is revised over time. The API documentation course and the AI courses are the main ones. These are the most substantive and most frequently updated parts of the site.
- **Blog posts** — dated essays and observations going back to 2006. Older posts reflect the tools and assumptions of their moment; check the date before treating a post as current guidance.

Content is authored in Markdown and published with Jekyll. Everything is free to read. Full text of every page is available at its URL; there is no paywall or login.

> **Markdown Endpoints**: Every post and topic has a clean Markdown mirror available by appending `.md` to its URL (for example, `https://idratherbewriting.com/blog/new-books-tech-comm-2026.md`).

## Start here

- [Home / latest blog posts]({{ site.url }}/): Reverse-chronological list of recent posts
- [About Tom Johnson]({{ site.url }}/aboutme/): Background, career, and what this blog covers
- [Documenting APIs course]({{ site.url }}/learnapidoc/): A 17-chapter course on writing API documentation, with hands-on activities
- [AI courses hub]({{ site.url }}/ai/index.html): Three self-contained courses on AI and technical communication
- [Series index]({{ site.url }}/series/): Multi-part post series grouped by topic

## Documenting APIs course

A free, book-length course on API documentation for technical writers and engineers. Covers REST API concepts, using an API like a developer, documenting endpoints, the OpenAPI specification, testing docs, conceptual topics, code tutorials, publishing, and career topics. Includes hands-on activities against real APIs. The chapters are listed below, and every individual topic is listed in the courses-and-pages index under Full archive indexes.
{% for folder in docapis.folders %}
- [{{ folder.title }}]({{ folder.landing | prepend: site.url }}): {% if folder.tiledesc %}{{ folder.tiledesc | strip_newlines | strip | replace: "&mdash;", "—" | replace: "&ndash;", "–" | replace: "&amp;", "&" | replace: "&#39;", "'" | replace: "&quot;", '"' | replace: "&nbsp;", " " }}{% else %}{{ folder.description | strip_newlines | strip | replace: "&mdash;", "—" | replace: "&ndash;", "–" | replace: "&amp;", "&" | replace: "&#39;", "'" | replace: "&quot;", '"' | replace: "&nbsp;", " " | truncate: 220 }}{% endif %}
{%- endfor %}

## AI and technical communication

Three self-contained courses. They don't build on each other. Written at different times, tracking the field's progression: use cases (2023), prompt engineering (2024), agent skills (2025-2026).

- [AI courses hub]({{ site.url }}/ai/index.html): Overview of all three courses and how they fit together
- [AI Book Club]({{ site.url }}/ai-book-club/): Notes and discussion on books about AI
- [All AI-related blog posts]({{ site.url }}/category-ai/): Dated posts on AI and tech comm

### Course: Agent skills

Building reusable instruction files that program an AI agent to handle repeatable documentation tasks. Includes a chapter on product skills — skills that route AI agents through your product's docs.

{%- endfor %}{% endfor %}

### Course: Prompt engineering for tech comm scenarios

Prompting techniques worked out against scenarios technical writers actually face: meeting notes, release notes, code samples, templates, and more.
{% for folder in prompteng.folders %}{% for item in folder.folderitems %}
- [{{ item.title | replace: "&mdash;", "—" | replace: "&ndash;", "–" | replace: "&amp;", "&" | replace: "&#39;", "'" | replace: "&quot;", '"' }}]({{ item.jurl | prepend: site.url }})
{%- endfor %}{% endfor %}

### Course: Use cases for AI

A survey of where AI genuinely helps with documentation work — summarizing, comparing, explaining code — and where it still falls short.

## Full archive indexes

This file lists the courses and recent posts. These secondary indexes list everything else, so together they cover every page on the site. Each one fits in a single fetch.

- [Courses, series, and pages]({{ site.url }}/llms/pages.txt): Every course topic, series page, and standalone page, grouped by section
{%- comment %}Each year needs a stub file at llms/posts-YYYY.txt. Copy last year's stub when the first post of a new year goes up. Years listed in splityears have two stubs instead (posts-YYYY-1.txt and posts-YYYY-2.txt), because one file would be too long for a single fetch.{% endcomment %}
{%- assign splityears = "2007,2009" | split: "," %}
{%- assign newestyear = site.posts.first.date | date: "%Y" | plus: 0 %}
{%- for y in (2006..newestyear) reversed %}{% assign ys = y | append: "" %}
{%- if splityears contains ys %}
- [Blog posts from July to December {{ y }}]({{ site.url }}/llms/posts-{{ y }}-2.txt)
- [Blog posts from January to June {{ y }}]({{ site.url }}/llms/posts-{{ y }}-1.txt)
{%- else %}
- [Blog posts from {{ y }}]({{ site.url }}/llms/posts-{{ y }}.txt)
{%- endif %}
{%- endfor %}
